definition: Multimodal learning is a type of deep learning that integrates and processes multiple types of data, referred to as modalities, such as text, audio, images, or video.
details: This integration allows for a more holistic understanding of complex data, improving model performance in tasks like visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, text-to-image generation, aesthetic ranking, and image captioning. Multimodal learning was proposed in 2011 at the beginning of the deep learning period. Large multimodal models, such as Google Gemini and GPT-4o, have become increasingly popular since 2023, enabling increased versatility and a broader understanding of real-world phenomena.

explainer.lead: Multimodal learning is deep learning that integrates and processes multiple data types such as text, audio, images and video. It matters because combining modalities gives a more holistic understanding and better task performance.

tiers.eli5: It is like studying for an exam using the textbook, a video and a podcast together instead of just one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train models jointly on multiple modalities to improve tasks like visual question answering and cross-modal retrieval. A pitfall is uneven data availability across modalities, which skews what the model learns.
tiers.paperLevel: Deep learning that integrates and processes multiple modalities, proposed in 2011 at the start of the deep learning period, improving tasks including visual question answering, cross-modal retrieval, text-to-image generation, aesthetic ranking and image captioning. Limits: depends on aligned multimodal data.

explainer.example: A model trained on paired images and captions learns to answer questions about a picture and to retrieve images matching a text query.
